s01-title: Video fourteen: WebAssembly. Tenant formulas, running in a sandbox.
s02-rust: The formula is a pure Rust function: it takes weight, zone, service and COD, returns a fee. It compiles to four hundred twenty-one bytes: no standard library, no I O, only computation. The tenant uploads the file like any other document.
s03-rule: In a Pricing Rule, saving means a test run in the sandbox. The hook prices a sample order; a module that fails to run is never saved.
s04-onoff: Same B2B order: rule off, seventy-three thousand. Rule on, no deploy or restart: fifty-one thousand. By hand: forty-five thousand, minus twenty percent, plus thirty percent for Express, plus the COD fee, rounded up to fifty-one thousand.
s05-order: In the Desk, the order shows who priced it: fifty-one thousand dong, by rule one, Wasm. The hook sets the fee and source; users can't edit them.
s06-runaway: A hostile script: an infinite loop. On save, it is rejected after fifty milliseconds and never switched on. The next order is still priced normally.
s07-limits: Chicory runs WebAssembly in pure Java. One mebibyte memory cap, no host imports, no I O or network, a fresh instance per call. Each rule sets a deadline, at most two hundred milliseconds.
s08-honest: To be accurate: Chicory can't count instructions yet, so CPU is time-capped. Tier one is on the roadmap.
s99-recap: Recap: tenants write formulas in Rust, checked on save, switched on without a deploy; infinite loops stop at fifty milliseconds. Next: MCP.
s10-outro: Astra. One platform, every business process. Open source, MIT license.
